## TL;DR

I closed the two report-state gaps that remained after #1041: a retry is now accepted only after its pending status has been persisted, and a persisted `done` status without a readable summary report is resolved as `failed` with the underlying file error. I also added a drawer fixture that seeds and renders a post-merge summary in the Report pane and declared a matching shot.

## Work and rationale

The prior review reports explain why the distinction between an old report and a newly queued run matters. A retry leaves the previous `summary.md` in place so that the generator can restore it if the new run fails. That means the status transition is the signal that a new run has started. The queue previously ignored the result of writing `pending`, started generation regardless, and returned no result to the route. When the status write failed, the old `done` state and report could still look successful to a client.

I changed `queueTaskSummary` to return whether a run was accepted. It returns false if it cannot persist `pending`, and in that case does not start the generation promise. Existing in-flight work is accepted only when the disk state is still `pending`. The retry route now returns 503 with an actionable message when queueing fails, so the CLI cannot proceed to poll an unchanged old `done` or `idle` state after a rejected queue. The status writer already retries its write once before reporting failure; this behavior remains the source of the surfaced persistence error.

For `done` status validation, the status reader now attempts to read the exact report file and returns a failed status containing the OS error if that read fails. It also treats an empty report as unusable. This ensures API and CLI consumers get a terminal failed state and meaningful reason. The drawer’s summary block already renders when the effective state is failed, including when the markdown is absent, so this failed response displays the error and retry guidance.

To cover the evidence gap, I added a preview fixture `drawer:postMergeSummary`. The task drawer’s fixture-aware fetch path seeds concise valid summary markdown and marks it done, avoiding a nonexistent server task lookup during capture. The shot declaration targets the Agent tab’s Report pane for the fixture task.

Tests were updated to assert that pending-write failure returns false, and added for a persisted `done` state with a missing report becoming failed with a reason. The required scoped RepoOS check is running; its result is recorded separately in the task transcript.

## Approaches tried

I first read the #1041 review-12 through review-14 reports and confirmed the relevant code was not fully fixed in this branch. The earlier feature work had already added two status write attempts and some stale-pending recovery, so I kept those mechanisms and made queue acceptance depend on their result instead of introducing a new status protocol or deleting the old report before retrying.

For the stale-report retry case, I considered whether the polling helper needed a new run identifier. The retry route writes `pending` synchronously before returning 202, so a successful queue changes the state clients poll. Making the route reject queue failures closes the unchanged-state path without widening the API payload or adding a second freshness token.

For the evidence state, I reused the existing preview fixture mechanism and task id rather than relying on engineering report history or a live summary file. This makes the Report pane capture deterministic and self-contained.

## Challenges and blockers

The engineering check runs remotely and takes longer than a local unit test because it uploads the checkpoint, installs dependencies, builds the app, and runs scoped tests. At report-draft time it had progressed through dependency installation and TypeScript compilation toward the UI build; I waited for the final verdict before handoff.

The `repoos update 1044 --shots` command reported that it was reading the main checkout’s board. The user explicitly restricted access to that checkout. I did not run further board commands. The source fixture and shot arguments were prepared, but the command’s board target means the task-worktree copy may not contain that declaration; this needs to be checked in the RepoOS handoff flow.

## Key learnings

For this feature, a committed report is not enough to establish that a retry succeeded. The synchronous pending-state write and the asynchronous report generation form one acceptance boundary: if the former fails, the latter must not start and clients must not be invited to poll an old report.

Likewise, a stored `done` value is only meaningful while its report remains readable. Returning the file-system reason from the status read keeps the CLI and drawer aligned and gives a human a useful retry path.
